subject: Session burst morphology and commitment mindmap
messages:
From: Alex Sato <alex.sato@photonai.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: sizing help for pilot (token shapes + bursts)

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this call last week. PhotonAI is kicking off a 6-week pilot next month and we need a pragmatic sizing recommendation so we can commit to a modest reserved pool. High level:

- Traffic today (beta): ~1.2M prompts/day, peak burst windows ~10 minutes during business hours.
- Prompt mix: 60% short queries (avg 18 tokens), 30% mid-length (avg 120 tokens), 10% long generation (avg 900 tokens).
- Session behavior: many short-lived interactive sessions (user sends 2–3 prompts then leaves), but a small proportion (~2%) are long-running multi-turn flows that keep KV cache hot.
- P99 target: 250–350 ms for short queries; 800–1,200 ms acceptable for long gens.

We'd like a short "mindmap" view that maps: concurrency buckets, burst headroom, suggested GPU SKUs and an ops play for graceful fallback (e.g., quantized variant or lower-capacity routing). Can you also flag which metrics we should export to help you size the fleet (session duration distribution, KV cache hit ratios, token/second of each route)?

Cc'ing procurement for timing — they may ask about billing cadence and commitment banding.

Appreciate any quick template you can send.

Best,
Alex
VP Product
PhotonAI

Subject: Re: Quick: sizing help for pilot (token shapes + bursts)

Hi Alex — great context, thanks. Attaching a compact sizing template (CSV) to make the inputs explicit and speed the sizing pass. Quick clarifying Qs before we build the mindmap:

1) Burst definition: when you say "10 minute" peak windows, do those usually have a ramp (gradual increase over 2–3 minutes) or sharp spikes?
2) Multi-turn flows: for the 2% long sessions, what's the average turn count and average response length? Do those flows keep KV cache across unrelated users or are they single-user long sessions?
3) Failure tolerance: during peak, is it acceptable to route long gens to a lower-cost quantized model with async fallback, or must consistency be identical to the hosted model?
4) Telemetry: can you share a 7-day export with fields -- timestamp, route_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, session_id, latency_ms (p50/p95/p99) and a boolean for kv_cache_hit? That will let us compute occupancy and queueing safely.

I asked Marissa and Karthik to help turn the CSV into a visual mindmap and a short ops checklist (fallback playbook + monitoring knobs).

If you can drop the 7-day export into the Drive link below, we can turn around a first draft by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: draft mindmap & shortlist (PHOTON pilot)

Grace / Karthik — rough internal notes for the reply I can send to Alex:

- High level recommendation: reserve N GPUs (TBD) sized for sustained baseline = 25% of average daily throughput with burst headroom = 2x baseline for 10-minute windows. Map GPUs to model variants:
  * baseline small: int8 quantized variant for 60% short queries (latency p50 ~80ms on A10x-type SKUs)
  * mid profile: mixed fp16/amp for 30% mid-length (SLO p95 300–400ms)
  * long-gen profile: fp16 on high-memory SKUs (V100-class or A100-L-type) with prewarmed KV cache for expected 2% long sessions

- Session-affinity: recommend sticky sessions for long-running flows to avoid KV cold starts; timeframe: 10–30 minutes TTL depending on user behavior.

- Telemetry knobs: token/sec per GPU, active sessions per GPU, avg KV cache occupancy, queue depth, p99 latency per route.

- Fallback playbook: route to quantized variant first, if queueing > X then degrade long-gens to a background async job + ticket the user, use region/fallback to cheaper region only for non-sensitive data.

I'll craft a one-page mindmap PDF and a short "next steps" checklist for Alex. Grace, if you want to add or change any of the assumptions above, call it out and I'll fold into the send.

—Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
(attachment: none)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood-inference.com>, procurement@photonai.com
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: PHOTON pilot: sizing mindmap + suggested commit bands

Hi Alex — thanks again. Attached is a 1-page sizing mindmap and short notes with a recommended commit band for the pilot. Highlights:

- Baseline sizing: reserve 6 x A10x-family GPUs to cover steady-state interactive traffic (assumes 1.2M prompts/day, token mix as you shared).
- Burst headroom: autoscale policy to allow +4 GPUs during 10-minute peaks (2x baseline burst capacity).
- Long-gen handling: 2 hot high-memory GPUs (A100-L-type) pinned for long sessions to keep KV cache hot; route long gens to these nodes with session affinity TTL = 20 mins.
- Cost/ops play: prefer int8 quantized variant for short queries; mid-length uses mixed-precision. On overload, degrade long gens to async batch with progress notification.

What we attached: photonai-sizing-mindmap.pdf (visual), map-notes.md (assumptions + table mapping token mix to expected tokens/sec), and a CSV template if you want to re-run numbers locally.

Next steps:
- If you can share the 7-day telemetry export (Drive link above), we will run an occupancy model and return a range-based SKU map (min/likely/max) within 24 hours.
- If procurement needs draft T&Cs for a 3-month reserved pilot, loop in the contract exec and we can provide a starter SOW + commitment band options.

Available for a 30-min sync this afternoon if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
